transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (CSM); Marcus Lee (Novaflow VP Eng), Priya Kumar (SRE), Dana Ortiz (CTO), Evan Cho (Platform)

Summary:
Quick follow-up to the escalation postmortem we circulated last week. Focus on fixes shipped, outstanding mitigations (cache warming, autoscale tuning), and next steps for a short Dedicated pilot to validate reliability under Novaflow peak patterns. Some transcription artifacts and names may be slightly off.

Topics covered:
- Root cause recap (KV cache eviction + bursty traffic + fallback path causing high latency)
- Immediate mitigations shipped (rollbacks, prefix caching, rate limiting tweaks)
- Longer-term mitigations (Dedicated reserve, canary rollout, runbook changes)
- Security/compliance notes (audit logs, KMS usage, data residency)
- Pilot plan and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: okay thanks everyone for joining, uh quick follow-up on the Novaflow incident. we have about 40 minutes, we wanted to run through the postmortem and next steps. Lina, can you give the engineering recap?
[00:32] Lina: yeah sure, um so root cause as we laid out is the combination of an aggressive cache eviction pattern on Novaflow's side plus an unexpected traffic spike at 09:14 UTC which caused a lot of cold kv cache misses. that cascaded into the fallback behavior where the request went to the higher latency model variant; then some autoscale cooldown timers didn't keep up. the net result was token latencies spiking to 6-8x normal for ~12 minutes.
[01:10] Priya: yeah that matches what we saw; our dashboards showed queueing on the inference layer and timeouts at the edge. we also had a couple of retries from client side which amplified the load.
[01:40] Lina: right, and to be clear the cache is a prefix/kvcache, i think sometimes transcriptions show it as k v c a c h e or kv-cache its the same thing. we shipped a hotfix that pins the prefix cache for the hot routes and adjusted the eviction window from 30s to 5m so warmup is much faster.
[02:10] Marcus: can you clarify which routes are 'hot'? is it only the payment-authorization flow? because we have a few flows that spike during batch jobs.
[02:35] Lina: good question — initial hot routes are payment-auth, recommendations inbound, and the internal webhook. we want to work with Novaflow to confirm the top-5 by RPS so we can pre-warm.
[03:00] Samir: we also toggled a short-term rate limit on the public api that prevents the retry storm — that was in place for the 45 minutes after the incident.
[03:20] Priya: that helped, thanks. one thing we saw though is that during the high tail latencies, the fallback variant selection sent a subset of requests to a larger model hosted in a different region, which spiked egress and introduced a cross-region variance. can we pin region routing?
[03:45] Lina: yes we can. Redwood has smart routing policies — by default we prefer lowest latency region, but in your account we can pin routes to single region or set a policy preference. for the pilot we recommend pinning to corp-us-west and setting a cost-based fallback only in emergencies.
[04:10] Dana: on the Dedicated vs hosted question — we need to understand tradeoffs. Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk but adds cost and ops. is the pilot a short Dedicated reservation or a short-burst dedicated pool?
[04:35] Samir: the short Dedicated pilot we discussed is a time-boxed reserved pool (2-4 GPUs depending on workload) with autoscale policies tuned for your peak. it's not a long contract — it's a pilot commit to validate stability. we'll show cost scenarios.
[04:57] Evan: what's the expected improvement in p95 latency if we do Dedicated plus cache warmup?
[05:15] Lina: based on our bench, for your model family and avg seq len, we expect p95 to drop from the incident 1.2s to ~180-250ms for hot routes when cached; tail improvements depend on batching and KV cache hit rate. we noted that quantization/precision changes had minor effect vs the cache and routing.
[05:45] Marcus: you mentioned runbook changes — what specifically?
[06:00] Ravi: we updated the runbook with explicit pre-warm steps, an autoscale cooldown adjustment, and an emergency rollback flow to hammer down fallback to hosted-lite models. Lina is drafting that now.
[06:25] Priya: we need more explicit metrics in the runbook — like key indicators (cache miss rate > 5%, sustained queue depth > 50) before throttling. can that be formalized?
[06:45] Lina: yes we'll include thresholds and playbook steps.
[07:10] Samir: security/compliance quick note — the incident did not touch logs with pii, and all egress stayed within your region except the fallback requests we called out. for KMS, your existing CMK is used for model artifacts and there were no key rotations during outage. Dana, any legal/SOC asks?
[07:40] Dana: we want an audit trail of who changed routing policies and when. also can Redwood provide a signed statement that postmortem mitigations were applied?
[07:55] Samir: yes we can provide a mitigation attestation and detailed audit log export for the incident window. that'll be added to the postmortem doc.
[08:15] Priya: about monitoring — can Redwood expose token-level tracing for our top routes? we need to correlate model latency with upstream queuing.
[08:35] Lina: yes we have token-level tracing but it has a cost and retention tradeoff; we can enable for a narrow window for you during the pilot. also the console has per-route p95/p99 which you can hook into.
[09:00] Marcus: what's the plan for canary/rollout? we want to ensure we don't regress during rollout of the cache changes.
[09:20] Lina: proposed plan: 1) replicate peak traffic in test with representative traces, 2) enable prefix pre-warm for top-5 routes in staging, run 2 hours of soak, 3) small canary on 5% traffic for 1 hour, measure latencies and error rates, 4) progressive ramp to 30-100% with guarded rollback. the canary will live for the Dedicated pilot as well.
[10:00] Evan: can Redwood script the pre-warm? having an automated pre-warm before peak job would be ideal.
[10:15] Lina: yes we can script via the Redwood API — a simple warmup script that issues synthetic requests to populate KV cache. we'll share sample script.
[10:35] Priya: about the fallback to larger model variant — can we change policy so fallback is to same-region, smaller-precision variant rather than cross-region big model?
[10:55] Lina: yes that's a policy tweak; it's supported. we just need to validate quality impact. for some prompts precision matters, so we recommend a test harness to verify outputs for those flows.
[11:20] Marcus: any concerns about data residency? some of our customers must keep data in eu-west and we have mixed traffic.
[11:35] Samir: we can set per-route region enforcement and your account can restrict routes by region; for EU traffic we can run Complementary region and ensure KMS keys are region-scoped. we'll include migration steps in the doc.
[12:00] Priya: one minor thing — the autoscaler cooldown default was 120s; that seems long for these surges. what's safe to change it to without oscillation?
[12:20] Lina: we recommend 45-60s for your workload with the Dedicated pool since we don't expect ephemeral spikes to be as frequent; combined with prefix warmup it reduces cold starts.
[12:40] Dana: okay let's talk pilot metrics — what are success criteria?
[12:55] Samir: proposed pilot success criteria: p95 for top-5 routes < 300ms under 95th percentile peak traffic for 2 hours; no >1% error rate; no cross-region egress for pinned routes. also confirm runbook executes within 10 minutes.
[13:20] Marcus: sounds reasonable. timeline?
[13:30] Samir: we suggested pilot the week of 2027-07-19, with Redwood delivering updated runbook and mitigation attestation by 2027-07-16.
[13:45] Priya: we can provide a traffic trace by tomorrow, 2027-07-14.
[13:55] Samir: perfect. action items recap will be in the notes.
[14:10] Lina: quick note about cost — Dedicated pilot will have an upfront pro-rated fee; we'll include options for burst vs reserved. if you choose reserved, we can give a short-term pilot price.
[14:30] Evan: would A/B tests on routing policies be possible to measure quality differences?
[14:45] Lina: yes we can route a small percentage to alternate policy and capture evals. integrate with Redwood Optimize to get model/quantization suggestions if needed.
[15:00] Marcus: any long-term reliability improvements beyond what we already covered?
[15:15] Lina: longer-term: smarter placement of model shards, better kernel selection for your sequence lengths, and a specialized batching strategy that prioritizes hot routes. those are multi-sprint items.
[15:35] Dana: for the governance ask, we need the audit logs and the signed mitigation ack. please include both in the postmortem doc.
[15:50] Samir: yes, we'll attach both.
[16:05] Ravi: scheduling note — follow-up check-in 30 minutes on 2027-07-27 proposed; we'll send invite.
[16:20] Priya: thanks, one last question: does Redwood provide a SLA credit for incidents like this?
[16:35] Samir: per your contract there's an SLA clause; this incident is within scope for investigation and remediation. if we determine an SLA breach, we'll follow the credit process. Samir: we'll raise to ops and legal if needed.
[16:55] Marcus: ok thanks everyone.

[17:05] Quick wrap and recap:
- Redwood: updated runbook, mitigation attestation, canary/pilot infra, sample pre-warm script, pricing options for Dedicated pilot.
- Novaflow: provide traffic trace and peak window logs, confirm top-5 hot routes, sign up for pilot account.
- Schedule follow up 2027-07-27 for pilot readout.

References shared during call: postmortem doc link (internal), runbook draft (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), sample pre-warm script (link).

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., kv cache spelled differently), and speaker labels sometimes generic.

End of transcript.
